sentences: VC-dimension and Littlestone dimension measure the complexity of a binary concept class for statistical and online learning respectively.
When the class is listed explicitly, the motivating question asks whether either dimension can be approximated within any constant factor in polynomial time.
The source answers this negatively under specified complexity assumptions through reductions from an unbalanced biclique problem.
Under stronger assumptions it obtains hardness even for approximation factors smaller than logarithmic in the input size.
This record captures a question answered conditionally within its cited paper, showing that even coarse evaluation of a class's learning complexity can be computationally difficult.
